claim: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing is a powerful approach to study microbiomes in an unbiased manner.
source: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing is a powerful approach to study microbiomes in an unbiased manner and of increasing relevance for identifying novel enzymatic functions.
evidence: This is a general statement about the capabilities of shotgun metagenomic sequencing, drawing from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: The potential of metagenomics to relate microbiome composition to function has been underutilized.
source: However, the potential of metagenomics to relate from microbiome composition to function has thus far been underutilized.
evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of the field based on the authors' perspective and inference from existing literature.

claim: MetaGPA is a framework that allows linking genetic information in metagenomes with a dedicated functional phenotype.
source: Here, we introduce the Metagenomics Genome-Phenome Association (MetaGPA) study framework, which allows linking genetic information in metagenomes with a dedicated functional phenotype.
evidence: This claim describes the novel method developed in this study, supported by the experimental data and results presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: MetaGPA was applied to identify enzymes associated with cytosine modifications in environmental samples.
source: We applied MetaGPA to identify enzymes associated with cytosine modifications in environmental samples.
evidence: This describes the specific application of the method in this study, supported by the experimental design and data presented.

claim: 2365 genes met the significance criteria in the MetaGPA study.
source: From the 2365 genes that met our significance criteria, we confirm known pathways for cytosine modifications and proposed novel cytosine-modifying mechanisms.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: MetaGPA confirmed known pathways for cytosine modifications.
source: From the 2365 genes that met our significance criteria, we confirm known pathways for cytosine modifications and proposed novel cytosine-modifying mechanisms.
evidence: This is supported by the identification of known enzymes like thymidylate synthase and DNA ligase in the results.

claim: A novel nucleic acid-modifying enzyme, 5-hydroxymethylcytosine carbamoyltransferase, was identified and characterized.
source: Specifically, we characterized and identified a novel nucleic acid-modifying enzyme, 5-hydroxymethylcytosine carbamoyltransferase, that catalyzes the formation of a previously unknown cytosine modification, 5-carbamoyloxymethylcytosine, in DNA and RNA.
evidence: This is supported by experimental validation including LC-MS analysis and enzymatic assays presented in Figure 6.

claim: 5-carbamoyloxymethylcytosine is a previously unknown cytosine modification.
source: Specifically, we characterized and identified a novel nucleic acid-modifying enzyme, 5-hydroxymethylcytosine carbamoyltransferase, that catalyzes the formation of a previously unknown cytosine modification, 5-carbamoyloxymethylcytosine, in DNA and RNA.
evidence: This is supported by LC-MS data and fragmentation patterns showing the novel modification.

claim: 5-hydroxymethylcytosine carbamoyltransferase catalyzes the formation of 5-carbamoyloxymethylcytosine in both DNA and RNA.
source: Specifically, we characterized and identified a novel nucleic acid-modifying enzyme, 5-hydroxymethylcytosine carbamoyltransferase, that catalyzes the formation of a previously unknown cytosine modification, 5-carbamoyloxymethylcytosine, in DNA and RNA.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing activity on both DNA and RNA substrates as shown in Figure 6.

claim: Advances in next-generation sequencing technology have been reshaping metagenomics.
source: Advances in next-generation sequencing technology have been reshaping metagenomics, making it possible to explore all microbes within a sample, including the overwhelming majority of those unculturable in standard growth conditions (Quince et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Quince et al., 2017.

claim: Next-generation sequencing makes it possible to explore microbes that are unculturable in standard growth conditions.
source: Advances in next-generation sequencing technology have been reshaping metagenomics, making it possible to explore all microbes within a sample, including the overwhelming majority of those unculturable in standard growth conditions (Quince et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Quince et al., 2017.

claim: Metagenomic analyses are being utilized across a broad spectrum of life science disciplines.
source: From studying human gut microbiome to marine viral communities (Sunagawa et al., 2015), metagenomic analyses are being utilized across a broad spectrum of life science disciplines, contributing to novel clinical diagnoses (Chiu and Miller, 2019), antibiotics and small molecule discovery (Hu et al., 2013; Charlop-Powers et al., 2014), food safety (Cao et al., 2017), biofuel generation (Hess et al., 2011), and environment stewardship (Nesme et al., 2014; Cavicchioli et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published work in various fields.

claim: Profiling taxonomic biodiversity is easier to answer than inferring biological functions in metagenomic studies.
source: Of the two primary questions metagenomic studies strive to address, profiling the taxonomic biodiversity – 'what is out there?' is easier to answer compared to inferring the biological functions – 'what do they do?'.
evidence: This is an inference based on the state of the field and the challenges described in the manuscript.

claim: There are many well-established strategies to quantify taxonomic diversity.
source: Indeed, there have been many well-established strategies to quantify taxonomic diversity such as analyzing known marker genes, binning contigs and assembling sequences into taxonomic groups or genomes (Sharpton, 2014; Quince et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sharpton, 2014 and Quince et al., 2017.

claim: A large fraction of the functional potential of microbiomes remains to be discovered.
source: However, a large fraction of the functional potential of microbiomes remains to be discovered.
evidence: This is an inference based on the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Microbiomes encode a large number of evolutionarily diverse genes coding for millions of peptides and proteins for distinctive functions.
source: Microbiomes encode a large number of evolutionarily diverse genes coding for millions of peptides and proteins for distinctive functions.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about microbial diversity.

claim: Functional diversity is particularly enormous for secondary metabolites and epigenetic modifications.
source: The functional diversity is particularly enormous for secondary metabolites and epigenetic modifications (Sharon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sharon et al., 2014.

claim: Environmental microbiomes are a plentiful source of DNA-modifying enzymes with diverse mechanisms.
source: Taking DNA modifications as an example , environmental microbiomes are a plentiful source of DNA-modifying enzymes with diverse mechanisms (Weigele and Raleigh, 2016; Hiraoka et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Weigele and Raleigh, 2016 and Hiraoka et al., 2019.

claim: In bacteriophages, DNA modifications are used to evade the restriction modification systems of the host bacterial cell.
source: In bacteriophages, DNA modifications are used to evade the restriction modification systems of the host bacterial cell.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about phage-host interactions.

claim: XP12 phage completely modifies cytosines in its genomic DNA to 5' methylcytosine.
source: Notably, a handful of bacteriophages have been described to completely modify cytosines in their genomic DNA, for example, 5' methylcytosine in XP12 phage (Kuo et al., 1968) and glycosylated 5' hydroxymethylcytosine in T4 phage (Revel and Georgopoulos, 1969).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kuo et al., 1968.

claim: T4 phage completely modifies cytosines in its genomic DNA to glycosylated 5' hydroxymethylcytosine.
source: Notably, a handful of bacteriophages have been described to completely modify cytosines in their genomic DNA, for example, 5' methylcytosine in XP12 phage (Kuo et al., 1968) and glycosylated 5' hydroxymethylcytosine in T4 phage (Revel and Georgopoulos, 1969).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Revel and Georgopoulos, 1969.

claim: Additional base modifications have been discovered including 5-(2-aminoethoxy)methyluridine, 5-(2-aminoethyl)uridine, and 7-deazaguanine.
source: Recently, additional base modifications have been discovered including 5-(2-aminoethoxy)methyluridine, 5-(2-aminoethyl)uridine, and 7-deazaguanine (Lee et al., 2018; Hutinet et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2018 and Hutinet et al., 2019.

claim: Current methods to harness functional potential of microbiomes mostly rely on computational prediction of gene function based on homology search.
source: Current methods to harness such functional potential of microbiomes, for the most part, came from computational prediction of gene function which is based on homology search to existing databases.
evidence: This is an inference about the current state of methods in the field.

claim: Homology searches often fail to impute the correct functions due to poor completeness and accuracy of microbial annotation.
source: Nonetheless, because of the poor completeness and accuracy of microbial annotation, homology searches often fail to impute the correct functions (Huson et al., 2009; Nayfach and Pollard, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Huson et al., 2009 and Nayfach and Pollard, 2016.

claim: Functional screens for novel functions require construction and high-throughput screening of a large number of clones which can be very time-consuming.
source: Novel functions can also be found using functional screens; however, such effort entails the construction and high-throughput screening of a large number of clones which can be very time-consuming (Martinez et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Martinez et al., 2004.

claim: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) combined with phylogenetic methods have been used to determine the genetic basis of phenotypes in specific bacteria.
source: For specific bacteria, determining the genetic basis of phenotypes has been addressed using genome-wide association studies (GWAS) (Falush and Bowden, 2006) combined with specific phylogenetic methods to account for the unique population structure of microbes (Collins et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Falush and Bowden, 2006 and Collins et al., 2018.

claim: Microbial GWAS have explored hundreds of isolates to identify genomic elements associated with antibiotic resistance, host specificity, or virulence.
source: Examples of microbial GWAS have explored hundreds of isolates to identify genomic elements that are statistically associated with, for example, antibiotic resistance (Chewapreecha et al., 2014), host specificity (Sheppard et al., 2013), or virulence (Laabei et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chewapreecha et al., 2014, Sheppard et al., 2013, and Laabei et al., 2014.

claim: Microbial GWAS studies are limited to known isolates and have not been extended to entire complex microbial communities.
source: Nonetheless, these studies are limited to known isolates and have not yet been extended to entire complex microbial communities.
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of existing methods.

claim: MetaGPA is conceptually close to GWAS as it associates genotypic data with phenotypic traits.
source: MetaGPA is conceptually close to GWAS as it associates genotypic data with phenotypic traits.
evidence: This is a comparison based on the conceptual framework of the method.

claim: MetaGPA uses association analyses at the level of protein domains rather than sequence variations as genetic markers.
source: Contrasting with microbial GWAS which uses sequence variations as genetic markers, MetaGPA incorporated association analyses at the level of protein domains to reveal genes that are significantly associated with the phenotype of interest.
evidence: This describes a key methodological difference supported by the experimental design.

claim: MetaGPA requires definition of a 'case' cohort and a 'control' cohort.
source: Like GWAS in individual species (Hirschhorn and Daly, 2005), MetaGPA requires definition of two cohorts, a 'case' cohort, that is, a group of organisms that share a specific phenotype under study in a given microbiome, and a 'control' cohort composed of all organisms within that microbiome (Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental design shown in Figure 1.

claim: Both cohorts in MetaGPA are sequenced independently, but all organisms included in a cohort are sequenced together without the need to isolate organisms.
source: While both cohorts are sequenced independently, all organisms included in a cohort are sequenced together without the need to isolate organisms.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The 'case' group is derived from the control group after applying a selection to only retain a given phenotype.
source: The 'case' group is derived from the control group after applying a selection to only retain a given phenotype.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the method.

claim: Unmodified cytosines are deaminated to uracils using APOBEC3A.
source: More specifically, unmodified cytosines are deaminated to uracils using the DNA cytidine deaminase apolipoprotein B mRNA editing enzyme catalytic polypeptide-like 3A (APOBEC3A) (Carpenter et al., 2012; Henry et al., 2009; Wijesinghe and Bhagwat, 2012), and subsequently excised by uracil-specific excision reagent (USER) (Bitinaite et al., 2007), resulting in fragmented DNA.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Carpenter et al., 2012, Henry et al., 2009, and Wijesinghe and Bhagwat, 2012.

claim: APOBEC3A deaminates 5-methyl-2'-deoxycytidine (5mdC) and, to a lesser degree, 5-hydroxymethyl-2'-deoxycytidine (5hmdC).
source: Because APOBEC3A also deaminates 5-methyl-2'-deoxycytidine (5mdC) and, to a lesser degree 5-hydroxymethyl-2'-deoxycytidine (5hmdC) (Sun et al., 2021), ten-eleven translocation dioxygenase 2 (TET2) and T4 phage β-glucosyltransferase (T4-BGT) can be used to protect 5mdC and 5hmdC prior to APOBEC3A treatment (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sun et al., 2021 and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: TET2 and T4-BGT can be used to protect 5mdC and 5hmdC prior to APOBEC3A treatment.
source: Because APOBEC3A also deaminates 5-methyl-2'-deoxycytidine (5mdC) and, to a lesser degree 5-hydroxymethyl-2'-deoxycytidine (5hmdC) (Sun et al., 2021), ten-eleven translocation dioxygenase 2 (TET2) and T4 phage β-glucosyltransferase (T4-BGT) can be used to protect 5mdC and 5hmdC prior to APOBEC3A treatment (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is part of the experimental design shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Enzymatic selection resulted in a 0.5% recovery of E. coli DNA and an average 35% recovery of T4gT DNA.
source: Compared to the original mock community, enzymatic selection resulted in a 0.5% recovery of E. coli DNA and an average 35% recovery of T4gT DNA (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment shown in Figure 2B.

claim: DNA containing modified cytosine is about 70-fold enriched compared to unmodified DNA.
source: This result shows that DNA containing modified cytosine is about 70-fold enriched compared to unmodified DNA.
evidence: This is calculated from the recovery rates presented in the data.

claim: At 1:1000 dilution, an average of 48.6% modified DNA was retained relative to no-enzyme control.
source: Even at 1:1000 dilution, an average of 48.6% modified DNA was retained relative to no-enzyme control.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the serial dilution experiment.

claim: Three environmental samples were collected from distinct sources: two from a sewage treatment plant and one from coastal sludge.
source: To explore the robustness of MetGPA, we included three environmental samples from distinct sources (Figure 3A); of the three samples, two were collected at a sewage treatment plant and the other one was collected from coastal sludge.
evidence: This describes the sample collection as shown in Figure 3A.

claim: 3901 modified contigs were identified from three DNA samples.
source: In total, 3901 modified contigs were identified from three DNA samples (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C-D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Distribution of contigs across all length ranges was equal between modified and unmodified contigs.
source: Distribution of contigs across all length ranges was equal between modified and unmodified contigs (Figure 3D) and the proportion of modified contigs among sewage and coastal samples were comparable (about 2% in both sewage samples and 3.5% in coastal total contigs) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The proportion of modified contigs was about 2% in both sewage samples and 3.5% in coastal total contigs.
source: Distribution of contigs across all length ranges was equal between modified and unmodified contigs (Figure 3D) and the proportion of modified contigs among sewage and coastal samples were comparable (about 2% in both sewage samples and 3.5% in coastal total contigs) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: 110 Pfam domain families were significantly associated with modified contigs (Bonferroni-corrected p-value < 0.01) representing a total of 2365 candidate genes.
source: From this composite dataset, we identified 110 Pfam domain families that were significantly associated with modified contigs (Bonferroni-corrected p-value < 0.01) representing a total of 2365 candidate genes.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the statistical analysis.

claim: None of the domains were found significantly associated with the case group in the control replicate experiment.
source: To estimate the false positive rate of association, we used our two control replicate experiments for which no selection has been done. We then performed a MetGPA analysis with one replicate being the control group and the other replicate being the 'case' group. From the 6737 protein domains assessed in MetaGPA, none of the domains were found significantly associated with the case group (data not shown).
evidence: This is a result from the control experiment to assess false positive rate.

claim: A subset of enzymes containing the thymidylate synthase domain have been shown to produce hydroxymethylpyrimidines.
source: For example, a subset of enzymes containing the thymidylate synthase domain (PF00303.20) have been shown to produce hydroxymethylpyrimidines (Neuhard et al., 1980).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Neuhard et al., 1980.

claim: DNA ligase and cytidine/deoxycytidylate deaminase are domains that have been found in DNA-modifying enzymes.
source: DNA ligase (PF14743.7, PF01068.22), and cytidine/deoxycytidylate deaminase (PF00383.24) are other domains that have been found in DNA-modifying enzymes (Bhattacharya et al., 1994; Subramanya et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bhattacharya et al., 1994 and Subramanya et al., 1996.

claim: Most of the carbamoyltransferase C-terminus domains from modified contigs form a distinctive phylogenetic branch.
source: Particularly, several domains, including carbamoyltransferase N-terminus (PF02543.16) and C-terminus (PF16861.6) domains, exhibited a clustered pattern in which most of the sequences from modified contigs formed a distinct phylogenetic clade from the other sequences (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is shown in the phylogenetic tree in Figure 4B.

claim: Complex DNA modifications in bacteriophages are usually carried out by multiple enzymes whose genes tend to cluster on the genome.
source: Complex DNA modifications in bacteriophages are usually carried out by multiple enzymes whose genes tend to cluster on the genome (Iyer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Iyer et al., 2013.

claim: The domains most frequently co-occurring with carbamoyltransferase C-terminus were carbamoyltransferase N-terminus, thymidylate synthase, phosphoribosyl-ATP pyrophosphohydrolase, dCMP deaminase Zn-binding region, and MafB19-like deaminase.
source: We found that, for example, the domains most frequently co-occurring with carbamoyltransferase C-terminus (PF16861.6) were carbamoyltransferase N-terminus (PF02543.16), thymidylate synthase (PF00303.20), phosphoribosyl-ATP pyrophosphohydrolase (PF01503.18), dCMP deaminase Zn-binding region (PF00383.24), and MafB19-like deaminase (PF14437.7) (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is shown in the co-occurrence analysis in Figure 4C.

claim: The co-occurrence of carbamoyltransferase and thymidylate synthase domains is only found in modified contigs.
source: For example, the co-occurence of carbamoyltransferase and thymidylate synthase domains is only found in modified contigs (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Three interaction cores were identified centered on thymidylate synthases, DNA ligases, and carbamoyltransferases.
source: Unbiased co-occurrence analysis was therefore conducted for the top 20 associated domain families. Indeed, significant positive correlations were observed, and the results demonstrated three interaction cores centered on thymidylate synthases, DNA ligases, and carbamoyltransferases, respectively (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is shown in the co-occurrence network in Figure 4D.

claim: Changing residue 177 from asparagine to aspartate can switch the preference of a canonical thymidylate synthase from dUMP to dCMP resulting in the formation of 5mdCMP.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that changing this residue from asparagine (Asn) to aspartate (Asp) can switch the preference of a canonical thymidylate synthase from dUMP to dCMP resulting in the formation of 5mdCMP (Graves et al., 1992; Hardy and Nalivaika, 1992; Liu and Santi, 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Graves et al., 1992, Hardy and Nalivaika, 1992, and Liu and Santi, 1992.

claim: The differential conservation score identifies position 177 and position 147 as the top two positions in thymidylate synthase.
source: Our differential conservation score identifies position 177 and position 147 (relative to E. coli thymidylate synthase) as the top two positions (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Both residues 147 and 177 are within the enzyme's active site.
source: Both residues are within the enzyme's active site (Figure 5C; Stout et al., 1998).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5C and supported by citation to Stout et al., 1998.

claim: Residues at positions 177 are mostly Asn for thymidylate synthase protein in the unmodified contigs.
source: As expected, residues at positions 177 are mostly Asn for thymidylate synthase protein in the unmodified contigs suggesting that dUMP is the substrate for these enzymes.
evidence: This is shown in the sequence alignment in Figure 5B.

claim: Thymidylate synthase proteins in the modified contigs have mostly Asp at position 177 consistent with modified cytosines.
source: Conversely, thymidylate synthase proteins in the modified contigs have mostly Asp position 177 consistent with modified cytosines (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is shown in the sequence alignment in Figure 5B.

claim: H147 forms a hydrogen bonding network through a water molecule to the keto oxygen of position 4 in dUMP.
source: The H147 forms a hydrogen bonding network through a water molecule to the keto oxygen of position 4 in dUMP (Matthews et al., 1990), suggesting a role in substrate specificity.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Matthews et al., 1990.

claim: Carbamoyltransferase domains are ranking within the top 20 most significant domains in the MetaGPA study.
source: Among the 110 domains that are significantly associated with DNA modifications, carbamoyltransferase domains are ranking within the top 20 most significant domains in our MetaGPA study (Figure 4A) and are exhibiting all three of our refinement metrics.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A.

claim: No carbamoyltransferases have been shown to act on any form of cytosine prior to this study.
source: Carbamoyltransferases are part of a large protein family catalyzing the addition of a carbamoyl group to various substrates but so far none of them has been shown to act on any form of cytosine, potentially revealing a new function and a new cytosine modification.
evidence: This is an inference based on existing knowledge about carbamoyltransferases.

claim: The co-occurrence of carbamoyltransferase and thymidylate synthase homologs specifically in modified contigs resembles the arrangement of the T4 phages.
source: The co-occurrence of carbamoyltransferase and thymidylate synthase homologs specifically in modified contigs (Figure 4C) resembles the arrangement of the T4 phages for which genes coding for the dCMP hydroxymethylase and β-glucosyltransferase co-occur on the genome (Miller et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with known phage systems, supported by citation to Miller et al., 2003.

claim: T4 dCMP hydroxymethylase is homologous to thymidylate synthase.
source: The T4 dCMP hydroxymethylase is homologous to thymidylate synthase and transfers a carbon from methyltetrahydrofolate (mTHF) to C5 of the pyrimidine ring producing an exocyclic methylene in the active site of the enzyme (Graves et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Graves et al., 1992.

claim: T4 β-glucosyltransferase transfers a glucose to the hydroxyl moiety of 5hmC.
source: Following incorporation of 5hmC into DNA during replication, T4 β-glucosyltransferase transfers a glucose to the hydroxyl moiety of 5hmC.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about T4 phage modification.

claim: Every substrate (carbamoyl phosphate, ATP, 5hmdC) and the enzyme were indispensable for the reaction.
source: The predicted reaction was tested by enzymatic assays and results showed that every substrate, namely carbamoyl phosphate, ATP, 5hmdC (genomic T4gt DNA was used as substrate in these experiments), and the enzyme were indispensable for the reaction (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Nearly 70% of 5hmdC were converted into 5cmdC in the denatured single-stranded T4gt genomic DNA.
source: Nearly 70% of 5hmdC were converted into 5cmdC in the denatured single-stranded T4gt genomic DNA.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the enzymatic assay.

claim: The activity of the carbamoyltransferase was several fold lower on double-stranded DNA, suggesting the preference of this enzyme for single-stranded DNA.
source: Interestingly, the activity of our carbamoyltransferase was several fold lower on double-stranded DNA, suggesting the preference of this enzyme for single-stranded DNA (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: When using synthesized single-stranded DNA oligo containing a single internal 5hmdC site as substrate, the conversion rate was nearly 100%.
source: When using synthesized single-stranded DNA oligo containing a single internal 5hmdC site as substrate, the conversion rate was nearly 100% (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6B.

claim: About 60% conversion of 5-hydroxymethyl-2'-deoxycytidine triphosphate (5hmdCTP) was observed.
source: LC-MS results demonstrated about 60% conversion of 5-hydroxymethyl-2'-deoxycytidine triphosphate (5hmdCTP) (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6C.

claim: No activity was seen for 5-methyl-2'-deoxycytidine triphosphate (5mdCTP) or 5-hydroxymethyl-2'-deoxyuridine triphosphate (5hmdUTP), indicating the carbamoyltransferase is specific to 5hmdCTP.
source: As expected, no activity was seen for 5-methyl-2'-deoxycytidine triphosphate (5mdCTP) or 5-hydroxymethyl-2'-deoxyuridine triphosphate (5hmdUTP), indicating the carbamoyltransferase is specific to 5hmdCTP.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The carbamoyltransferase is active on 5hmdCTP, opening up the possibility that the reaction could take place before the nucleotide is incorporated into the phage DNA.
source: The fact that the carbamoyltransferase is active on 5hmdCTP (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 3A) opens up the possibility that the reaction could take place before the nucleotide is incorporated into the phage DNA.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental results.

claim: A decrease in deamination rate was only observed in the T4gt genome indicating specific carbamoylation on 5hmdC.
source: We saw a decrease in deamination rate only in the T4gt genome indicating specific carbamoylation on 5hmdC.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6D.

claim: All combinations of NCN motifs containing 5hmdC displayed comparable deamination levels compared to the control library, suggesting a general binding mechanism with no preferred context.
source: Furthermore, all combinations of NCN motifs containing 5hmdC displayed comparable deamination levels compared to the control library, suggesting a general binding mechanism with no preferred context.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6D.

claim: 5cmC is formed during the reaction with RNA containing 5-hydroxymethylcytosine, albeit at much lower yields.
source: LC-MS and fragmentation pattern confirmed that 5cmC is formed during the reaction, albeit at much lower yields (Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 3B-C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 3B-C.

claim: Carbamoylation of free nucleotide 5-hydroxymethylcytidine triphosphate (5hmCTP) was detected.
source: Carbamoylation of free nucleotide 5-hydroxymethylcytidine triphosphate (5hmCTP) was also detected (Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The novel nucleic acid-modifying enzyme identified from MetaGPA studies acts on DNA, RNA, and nucleotide triphosphates.
source: We thus concluded that this novel nucleic acid-modifying enzyme identified from MetaGPA studies acts on DNA, RNA, and nucleotide triphosphates.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing activity on all three substrates.

claim: MetaGPA is cost effective and requires reduced efforts.
source: Being cost effective and requiring reduced efforts, MetaGPA essentially rests on two sequencing libraries derived from the same starting material: one library reflects all the organisms in the community while the other library results from a selection to only contain organisms with a phenotype of interest.
evidence: This is an inference about the practical advantages of the method.

claim: MetaGPA allows for candidate genes identification in less than a week.
source: This experimental setup allows for candidate genes identification in less than a week.
evidence: This is an inference about the time efficiency of the method.

claim: MetaGPA is phenotype-driven and the identification of candidate genes is agnostic to prior annotations.
source: Our MetaGPA study framework is phenotype-driven and the identification of candidate genes is agnostic to prior annotations.
evidence: This describes a key feature of the method.

claim: MetaGPA can be performed with any case/control cohort pair as long as distinct phenotypes can be partitioned through selection of the case cohort.
source: Theoretically, it can be performed with any case/control cohort pair as long as distinct phenotypes can be partitioned through selection of the case cohort.
evidence: This is speculation about the broader applicability of the method.

claim: The partitioning is crucial for MetaGPA to succeed and requires the development and optimization of the selection process for every new MetGPA application.
source: Nonetheless, this partitioning is crucial for MetaGPA to succeed and therefore requires the development and optimization of the selection process for every new MetGPA application.
evidence: This is an inference about the requirements for successful application of the method.

claim: The only reported carbamoylated nucleotide prior to this study is 5-carbamoylmethyluridine, which is located in the first position of the anticodon of yeast valine tRNA34.
source: To our knowledge, the only reported carbamoylated nucleotide is the 5-carbamoylmethyluridine, which is located in the first position of the anticodon of yeast valine tRNA34 (Yamamoto et al., 1985).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yamamoto et al., 1985.

claim: The 5cmdC modification is most likely found in a bacteriophage.
source: Given the co-occurrence on the same contig of phage-specific genes (such as phage tail genes) with the 5-hydroxymethylcytosine carbamoyltransferase gene characterized in this study, the 5cmdC modification is most likely found in a bacteriophage.
evidence: This is an inference based on the genomic context of the identified gene.

claim: All the cytosines in the phage containing the carbamoyltransferase are predicted to be modified.
source: Because of the nature of the MetaGPA selection and the fact that the carbamoyltransferase show no sequence specificity, we predict that all the cytosines in this phage are modified, possibly conferring the ability to escape most of the restriction digestion system found in bacteria.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental design and results.

claim: The modification may confer the ability to escape most of the restriction digestion system found in bacteria.
source: Because of the nature of the MetaGPA selection and the fact that the carbamoyltransferase show no sequence specificity, we predict that all the cytosines in this phage are modified, possibly conferring the ability to escape most of the restriction digestion system found in bacteria.
evidence: This is speculation about the biological function of the modification.

claim: The evolutionary advantage may explain the prevalence of this enzyme family in the phage fraction of all the microbiomes investigated in this study.
source: This evolutionary advantage may explain the prevalence of this enzyme family in the phage fraction of all the microbiomes investigated in this study.
evidence: This is speculation about the evolutionary significance of the finding.

claim: For scenarios where phenotypes are not physically coupled with DNA or RNA, selection will have to be done while preserving the integrity of cells and viral particles to retain the link between phenotype and genotype.
